decisions.reason: The navigation and observation camera builds directly on the firm's core optical and star-tracker know-how, and it kept a page of its own in both years, so the firm can interpret its results and improve it in-house.
The modular camera line has proven flight heritage on ESA's HERA mission, which gives strong learning feedback and builds on core competence, matching the firm's push toward flexible sensors.
The space situational awareness suite extends existing optoelectronic sensor knowledge into a growing market, and its continued dedicated page in both years signals ongoing commitment.

The miniaturized LiDAR builds on the firm's docking LiDAR heritage and fits its push toward smaller satellites, though its weaker website presence suggests it is still maturing, so it stays while R&D refines it.
The radiation-hard camera line is a natural extension of space-grade imaging expertise, newly launched with its own page, and has too little market evidence yet to justify withdrawal.
The asteroid navigation camera draws on the framing-camera knowledge proven on HERA, so the firm can absorb lessons from that mission, although its low visibility makes it somewhat less certain.
